events.title: Battle of Culloden
events.description: The Jacobite army of Charles Edward Stuart was decisively defeated near Inverness, Scotland, by government forces led by the Duke of Cumberland. The battle lasted less than an hour and was the last pitched battle fought on British soil.
events.significance: It ended the Jacobite risings and the Stuart claim to the British throne, and led to the suppression of the Highland clan system and traditional Gaelic culture.

events.title: First Passenger Train in India
events.description: The first passenger railway in India ran 34 kilometres from Bori Bunder in Bombay to Thane, carrying about 400 guests in 14 carriages hauled by three locomotives.
events.significance: It marked the start of the Indian railway network, which became one of the largest in the world and transformed the country's economy and mobility.

events.title: Harriet Quimby Flies the English Channel
events.description: American aviator Harriet Quimby became the first woman to pilot an aircraft solo across the English Channel, flying from Dover to Calais in a Blériot monoplane.
events.significance: Her flight was a landmark for women in aviation, though news coverage was overshadowed by the Titanic sinking the day before.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Writes 'Letter from Birmingham Jail'
events.description: While jailed for taking part in nonviolent protests against segregation in Birmingham, Alabama, King wrote an open letter answering eight white clergymen who had criticized the demonstrations as unwise and untimely.
events.significance: The letter became one of the most influential statements of the civil rights movement, defending nonviolent civil disobedience and the moral duty to oppose unjust laws.

events.title: Texas City Disaster
events.description: The cargo ship SS Grandcamp, loaded with ammonium nitrate fertilizer, exploded in the port of Texas City, Texas, setting off chain-reaction fires and further explosions that killed at least 581 people.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest industrial accident in United States history and led to major reforms in the handling and regulation of hazardous materials and in disaster response.
